title: SO-Arena separates accuracy from reliable decisions

lines: A margin note on SO-Arena is now in the Diary.

body:
The item reports that SO-Arena evaluates System One models that decide quickly without long token generation across 11 domains and five capability families. It combines evidence-grounded labels, sandboxed interactive evaluation, stability under option-set changes, and recognition of missing answers. Across 21 models, scaling and extra reasoning help unevenly; the strongest System One model ranks only seventh in reliability, suggesting that accuracy and dependable decision-making are separate dimensions.
Would the ranking remain the same under both stated reliability measures?
Would all 21 models have been evaluated consistently across the domains, capability families, and evaluation modes?
Is the separation between accuracy and dependable decision-making robust to scaling and additional reasoning?
